protocol.description:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.
This protocol allows a privileged DDE client such as the dock or shell to observe seat activity that the compositor detects: pointer button and wheel activity, and drag and drop lifecycle events, scoped to a given seat.
The compositor must reject bind attempts from non-privileged clients.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

interface.name: treeland_active_notify_manager_v1
interface.description:
A global that creates treeland_active_notify_v1 objects for privileged DDE clients. Each notifier reports activity for one seat; clients observing several seats create several notifiers.
The compositor must reject bind attempts from non-privileged clients.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_active_notify_manager_v1 object. Notifiers created through this manager are not affected.

request.name: get_active_notify

description.summary: create a new seat activity notifier

request.description: Create a new treeland_active_notify_v1 object that reports activity for the given seat. The seat must be a valid, current wl_seat.

interface.name: treeland_active_notify_v1
interface.description:
A notifier object reports seat activity that the compositor detects. Activity is reported as enter/leave events tagged with the source that triggered them.
The mouse and wheel sources have different semantics:
For mouse, enter and leave report the aggregate state of the left pointer button only. activity_enter is sent when the left button is pressed, activity_leave when it is released. Other pointer buttons do not generate these events. The compositor sends enter and leave as matched pairs: it must not send a second enter before the matching leave, nor a leave when the left button is not pressed.
For wheel, enter and leave are discrete per-event pulses, not a persistent state. activity_enter is sent for each wheel event whose angle delta is positive, and activity_leave for each whose angle delta is negative; the compositor may send several enter (or several leave) events in a row without an intervening opposite event. Clients must treat each wheel event independently and must not infer a lasting state from a single enter or leave.
The start_drag, drop, and drag_cancelled events report the lifecycle of a drag and drop operation on the seat. start_drag is sent when the operation begins. Exactly one terminal event follows each start_drag: drop when the operation completes with a successful drop, or drag_cancelled when the operation ends without a drop (for example because the drag was cancelled or the source destroyed). No further drag events are sent after the terminal event until the next start_drag.

enum.name: reason
enum.description: The input source that triggered an activity event. Used by the activity_enter and activity_leave events. See the interface description for the per-source semantics.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_active_notify_v1 object. The compositor stops reporting activity for the seat bound to this notifier.

event.name: activity_enter
event.description: For mouse, sent when the left pointer button is pressed. For wheel, sent for each wheel event whose angle delta is positive; the compositor may send several in a row without an intervening activity_leave. See the interface description for the per-source semantics.

event.name: activity_leave
event.description: For mouse, sent when the left pointer button is released. For wheel, sent for each wheel event whose angle delta is negative; the compositor may send several in a row without an intervening activity_enter. See the interface description for the per-source semantics.

event.name: start_drag
event.description: Sent when a drag and drop operation starts on the seat bound to this notifier. Exactly one terminal event (drop or drag_cancelled) follows each start_drag.

event.name: drop

description.summary: a drag operation completed with a drop

event.description: Terminal event for a drag and drop operation that completes with a successful drop on the seat bound to this notifier. No further drag events are sent after drop until the next start_drag.

event.name: drag_cancelled

description.summary: a drag operation ended without a drop

event.description: Terminal event for a drag and drop operation that ends without a drop, for example because the drag was cancelled or the drag source destroyed. No further drag events are sent after drag_cancelled until the next start_drag.
